To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the analysis of time series of counts following GLMs is possible in a robust way.

Outliers and intervention effects can be incorporated into a general class of models, which includes the classical ARIMA models, by using an appropriate specification of the conditional mean function.

the following modifications of GLMs are useful in the analysis of count data: 1) The introduction of a multiplicative outlier effect, 2) the introduction of an additive outlier effect, and 3) the introduction of a multipurpose intervention effect, that is, a multiplicative outlier and additive outlier effect combined.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a generalisation of the classical ARIMA models for time series of counts to a robust and adaptive class of models which allows for the detection, identification and modelling of outliers in time series of counts.
the analysis and the modelling of count time series with outliers and intervention effects in a generalised linear model setting.
the problem of outlier detection and robust estimation for time series of count data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
robustness is a desirable feature of a statistical model, but that robustness is not the same as robustness.
the problem of robust analysis and surveillance of count time series is not yet fully solved, and that further research is required.
robust methods are not only necessary but also sufficient to detect outliers and intervention effects in count time series.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that it is possible to model count time series in such a way that they can be used for retrospective and prospective analyses in a robust way, and that we can distinguish outliers of different types in such a model.
we have shown that it is possible to incorporate, detect, and to a certain extent distinguish between different types of outliers and interventions in count time series following GLMs.
we have developed a framework which is able to detect outliers and interventions, and which is able to distinguish between different types of outliers and interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of count data can be performed robustly, and that the robust analysis of count time data can be done in a way that it is comparable to the analysis of continuous data.
the problem of robust estimation of count time series is much more complex than in the case of linear models.

the problem of outlier detection in time series of counts is not just a problem of robust estimation of the model parameters, but rather a problem of robust parameter inference, which requires a more comprehensive approach.
